LIVING CONNECTOME · 01

It’s walking. You can interrupt a step.

A procedural male fruit fly walks a tripod gait while a real nerve-cord simulation — traced neuron by neuron from electron microscopy — drives one shin. Tripod walking itself is kinematic; the flex is neural.

01 — STIMULATE

Fold the front-left shin.

The fly is already walking. When the button lights up, press it — that leg’s shin is driven by BANC motor neurons for a moment, then the gait takes it back.

Then watch the reflex ↗ — bend the joint yourself and see the nerve cord push back. The better first lesson.

Kick writes 200 Hz straight onto the joint. Flex goes through the real motor neurons. Silencing sensors does nothing useful yet — those cells aren’t typed well enough to close the loop.

What am I looking at?

Male 3D mesh, female central nervous system. The cord is BANC v888 as a leaky integrate-and-fire model. Joints are kinematic, not physics. This is not a complete biological fly.
